scope: Pinned SDL3 TLS bridge with checked32-bit guest IDs and native storage.
storage: Guest SDL_TLSID memory holds an opaque nonreused token; native SDL_TLSID and native value snapshots remain host-owned. A process-qualified registry serializes ID creation. Real SDL_GetTLS/SDL_SetTLS provide native thread isolation.
cleanup: Registered native finalizers run before guest stack and TEB release on return, ExitThread and FreeLibraryAndExitThread paths, and after DLL detach callbacks. Explicit SDL_CleanupTLS and native SDL_Quit run inside live-owner CPU scopes. Guest destructors use cdecl and preserve caller registers and LastError; no saved borrowed CPU survives asynchronously.
semantics: Replacement does not invoke the old destructor.
A registered destructor runs for a zero guest value, matching the pinned native SDL cleanup loop.
Copied guest ID tokens address the same slot within their process.
Snapshots remain alive through the entire destructor pass so reads by subsequent callbacks do not dereference freed host value records.
Native SDL errors and allocation failures are returned rather than fabricated as success.
boundaries: TLS mutation or recursive cleanup during the pinned native cleanup loop stops explicitly.
Native cleanup outside a live owner scope cannot invoke guest destructors.
Cross-FLS/SDL resurrection cycles are not accepted; only the tested teardown ordering is established.
The ID registry has process lifetime; process restart in the same host is not implemented.
Component fixtures do not establish original game sound or thread-exit behavior in a running match.
